summary: Iteration 4: frontend retest of the 8 failures from iteration 3, plus regression checks. I tested at 1920x1080 and, for the worker workchat, at 390x844. 7 of 8 now pass: (1) workchat reaction picker and Reply for worker (desktop and mobile) and employer; (2) employer pinned section and composer; (3) Upcoming and Completed shift tabs; (4) All tab opens the direct chat; (5) inbox header and tabs sit above the list, and the employer's 4th tab is 'Workers'; (6) admin threads are grouped and the employer can open one and reply; (7) checkout worker names show and the stray 0 is gone. (8) FAILS: the worker Workchats tab still shows the raw giphy URL. While cleaning up I found a new backend bug: different emojis are treated as the same emoji, so reaction counts are wrong and tapping one emoji can remove another. I confirmed this in the database and with an API call. Regression checks that pass: payslip PDF download, employer direct chat react/reply/send, clock-in. I did not re-run the worker direct chat this round.

critical.issue: The emoji columns use utf8mb4_unicode_ci, which treats all 4-byte emojis as equal (SELECT '👍'='🙏' COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci returns 1). Result 1: GROUP BY message_id,emoji merges different emojis. Message 50 has 👍 (user 6) and 🙏 (user 9) but the API returns [{👍, count 2}]; message 55 has 🔥 and 👏 but shows '🔥 2'. Result 2: the toggle check `WHERE ... emoji=?` matches the wrong emoji. As the worker I POSTed 🙏 on message 50 and it DELETED my 👍. Result 3: the primary key (message_id,user_id,emoji) cannot hold two different 4-byte emojis from one user. Fix: ALTER both emoji columns to `VARCHAR(16) CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_bin` (also update the CREATE TABLE in user-message-routes.js:272 and the direct-reactions DDL), or add COLLATE utf8mb4_bin in the GROUP BY and WHERE clauses.

action_items: HIGH: Change the emoji columns of workchat_message_reactions and direct_message_reactions to COLLATE utf8mb4_bin (DDL and ALTER). The unicode_ci collation merges different emojis in GROUP BY and in the toggle WHERE.
HIGH: Fix contrast in the employer admin thread overlay: the title is white on white and the admin message text is near-white on light grey. Also keep the overlay open after sending a reply.
MEDIUM: In App.jsx line 812 (worker Workchats list), wrap w.last_message in previewText().

LOW: Hide Cancel shift on Completed shift cards. Style the checkout Approve button. Fix quoted-reply contrast in own bubbles. Show 'hyrz support' instead of the admin email in the worker admin thread.
critical_code_review_comments: user-message-routes.js:344 and :386-388: emoji GROUP BY and equality depend on the column collation. utf8mb4_unicode_ci and utf8mb4_general_ci compare all supplementary-plane emoji as equal.

App.jsx is still a 1646-line file with very long minified lines (one line holds a whole view), and worker and employer workchat views are duplicated (lines ~700 vs ~804, 733 vs 812). That is why fixes like previewText land in one branch and not the other. Extract a shared WorkchatList and WorkchatRoom component.
styles.css is 18,050 lines with many `html body #root ... !important` override layers (e.g. 14967-14982). The admin-thread contrast bug comes from conflicting override layers. Consolidate them.

rca of the issue: Emoji reactions: the MariaDB utf8mb4_unicode_ci collation gives all 4-byte emojis the same weight. Reproduce: as worker, POST /api/workchats/8/messages/50/reactions {emoji:'👍'}, then POST {emoji:'🙏'}. The second call deletes the 👍 instead of adding 🙏. GET also returns merged counts. Mitigation: use utf8mb4_bin on the emoji columns. GIF preview: the worker branch at App.jsx:812 never calls previewText.
